title: Simple QKD keyrate computations from tangent-line bounds
authors: Jun Hui Goh, Ernest Y. -Z. Tan
abstract: Recent work in quantum key distribution (QKD) has yielded finite-size keyrates based on convex optimisation problems, using the framework of entropy accumulation. Multiple solvers have been developed to address these optimisations in recent years, but have been based on a somewhat elaborate framework using sophisticated algorithms, in order to accommodate a broad range of QKD protocols. In this work, we note that for basic QKD protocols such as qubit BB84, the keyrates can be easily computed using off-the-shelf solvers instead, by obtaining suitable tangent lines to lower bound terms in the objective function. We compute the resulting finite-size keyrates and compare them to previous work. Moreover, we extend this approach to the six-state protocol, by deriving closed-form expressions for the single-round Rényi entropies in the protocol. This should facilitate subsequent study of the six-state protocol via entropy accumulation.
summary: This paper develops a computationally efficient method to calculate the finite-size keyrates for QKD protocols by reformulating the problem as a convex optimization solvable via tangent-line approximations. By applying this technique to BB84 and the six-state protocol, the authors provide certified lower bounds for the keyrate, simplifying complex calculations previously requiring elaborate solvers.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational challenge of finding certified lower bounds for the finite-size keyrates in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols.
main_result: The authors propose a tractable method using tangent-line approximations to compute these keyrates for basic protocols like BB84 and the six-state protocol, yielding results comparable to previous work.
method: The core method involves reformulating the keyrate calculation as a convex optimization problem and then employing tangent-line lower bounding techniques to solve it using off-the-shelf solvers.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to QKD protocols, specifically focusing on the qubit BB84 and the six-state protocol, analyzed in an entanglement-based setting.
key_observables: Finite-size keyrate ($\ell_{key}$), asymptotic keyrate ($	ext{r}_{asymp}$), and various Rényi entropy terms ($	ilde{H}_{\uparrow}^{\alpha}, 	ilde{H}_{\downarrow}^{\alpha}$).
important_parameters: The security parameter $\epsilon_{secure}$, the order of the Rényi entropy $\alpha$, and protocol-specific parameters like $Q_{thresh}$ and $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on obtaining suitable tangent lines to lower bound terms, which provides a guaranteed lower bound on the true keyrate.
figures_summary: Figures show the keyrate dependence on the number of tangent lines and the grid size, indicating that plateaus are reached when sufficient computational resources are used.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of keyrate computation, then details the tangent-line approximation method for simple protocols, and finally extends the approach by deriving closed-form expressions for the six-state protocol's Rényi entropies.
why_interesting: While focused on QKD, the mathematical techniques—convex optimization bounding via tangent lines—are highly relevant to finding rigorous bounds in complex quantum information tasks.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Keyrate as a function of the number of tangent lines. The grid search used to plot this graph was 40 × 40. The plot is not monotone because for each ntangent we took the tangent lines at uniformly spaced points over Q ∈[0, 1], which results in the set of tangent lines for each ntangent not being a subset of those for ntangent + 1.
FIG. 2. Plot of keyrate value as the grid size of the grid search increases. 100 tangent lines were used in the approximation of the convex optimisation.

FIG. 3. Plot comparing the achievable keyrate com- puted by the original authors to that computed by our proposed methodology, using the values of α and γ found in [1]. The purple graph plots the values com- puted by the original authors. The blue graph plots the val- ues computed using the proposed methodology, with the val- ues of α and γ found in [1]. The dashed black line shows the asymptotic keyrate for our parameter choices, which is rasymp = 0.663. We caution however that the results dis- played for n <∼104 (red region in figure) may correspond to significant abort probability during error correction; see Re- mark 1.
